discovery: Detection and characterization of exoplanet atmospheres through transit and eclipse spectroscopy

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: Drake Deming
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

motivation: The 2019 Prize recognised the discovery of planets around other stars. These nominees turned those planets into physical worlds that can be measured. Seager predicted that starlight filtered through a transiting planet's limb would carry absorption signatures of its atmosphere. Charbonneau observed the first transit of an exoplanet (HD 209458b) and in 2002 detected sodium in its atmosphere, the first measurement of an extrasolar planetary atmosphere. In 2005 Deming and Charbonneau independently measured thermal emission from hot Jupiters during secondary eclipse with Spitzer, giving direct temperatures and, later, day-night maps. From very small photometric signals, carefully calibrated against instrument systematics, they built a quantitative atmospheric physics of planets we cannot resolve. That work now underpins JWST's measurements of water, carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide. As with magnetometry at Enceladus, an indirect but careful measurement opened a new environment to physical understanding.
